title: ARC low-cost four-season dwelling and distributed utility package

source_record.provenance: Prior ARC design specification supplied to Living Region; the original quote/spreadsheet was not found in the current Living Region checkout, its git history, or the standalone ARC carrying-capacity checkout.
source_record.retrieval_note: Values are retained as a transparent planning package until original quotations or current procurement evidence are restored.

arc_household_systems.label: ARC household systems
arc_household_systems.description: Roof rainwater, household treatment/storage, household sanitation/greywater and off-grid electrical systems are part of the resident-owned dwelling package.

generic_distributed_alternatives.label: Generic well/septic/grid alternatives
generic_distributed_alternatives.description: Generic alternatives remain available for sites where the ARC package cannot be approved. They are not the legal-minimum ARC baseline.

centralized_shared_services.label: Centralized project services
centralized_shared_services.description: Use only when a project selects and designs centralized water, sewage or electrical infrastructure. Its capital belongs in shared infrastructure, not in the resident dwelling package.

components.label: Structure and envelope
components.derivation: Inclusive legacy completed-dwelling range less the separately specified heating, water/plumbing/sanitation, hot-water and electrical allocations. No independent structure quote was recovered.
components.design_basis: Four-season ARC dwelling envelope; replace with an as-designed bill of materials when available.

components.label: Heating appliance and system
components.derivation: Transparent allocation within the inclusive legacy range; the existing thermal model supplies heat demand but not a current appliance quote.
components.design_basis: Winter masonry-heater concept with thermosiphon hot-water integration; actual appliance, code and installation costs remain site/design-specific.

components.label: Water, plumbing and sanitation
components.design_basis: Roof rainwater collection; first flush; indoor food-grade storage; demand pump; sediment filtration; UV; under-sink reverse osmosis; compact PEX plumbing; sink and private shower; drainless composting toilet; permitted Class 2 greywater system under the applicable flow limit.
components.approval_note: Water source, potable treatment, sanitation and greywater approval remain site-specific and must be confirmed before construction.

components.label: Hot water
components.design_basis: Winter masonry-heater thermosiphon hot water and summer solar-thermal hot water.
components.approval_note: Plumbing, pressure, temperature and seasonal system design require code review.

components.label: Off-grid electrical system
components.design_basis: Approximately 400 Wh/day planning load; approximately 400 W PV; MPPT charge controller; approximately 2.52 kWh nominal flooded lead-acid storage; 1,000 W pure-sine inverter.
components.approval_note: Electrical design, battery safety and any ESA/utility requirements remain site-specific.

generic_alternatives.label: Generic well or approved water system
Generic septic or approved sewage system
Generic grid connection or electrical system

accounting_rules: Every household water, sanitation/greywater, hot-water and electrical component is included once in resident dwelling capital when arc_household_systems is selected.
Centralized services are alternatives in the shared-infrastructure layer and must not be combined with the corresponding household system component.
Land lease and shared infrastructure do not absorb resident dwelling utility capital.

The legacy approximately 11,230 CAD utility total reconciles to 11,240 CAD when the listed 5,940 + 2,000 + 3,300 component values are added; the 10 CAD difference is treated as source rounding, not hidden cost.
